Crying "Alas, alas!" He wandered about as if maddened with love: "Tell Me, why have You brought about such a calamity?
I am already half dead with grief of heart in the terrible separation from Gorachand.
Still I lived on, looking upon Your face. If You too have left — where shall I go now?"
Speaking thus and much more, the Lord lamented; not a drop of it could I write down.
Learning of Nityananda's disappearance, the devotees wept: "Where is Nityananda?"
Master Virabhadra, weeping, rolled in the dust, and Sri Advaitachandra consoled everyone.
He had preparations made for a great festival and sent invitations wherever the devotees were.
In due time all the mahantas came, and in Khardaha joy awoke once more.
On the day of the festival, having bathed, all together began a great sankirtana.
In seven groups fourteen madal drums resounded, and hundreds of sweet-sounding karatalas.
In each group one person danced, but the son of Kubera (Advaita) danced in all the groups.
As I saw that bliss of kirtana with my own eyes — so, for fear of length, I could not describe it.
After the sankirtana all the Sri Vaishnavas relished the sweetness of Gauranga's pastimes.
Then Master Virabhadra, having cleaned the place, carefully arranged three seats in one spot.
Setting out three offerings of food, he placed them there and began to speak to Sri Advaita:
"I will tell You one wish of mine: fulfil, Gosani, the desire of a child.
As formerly Mahaprabhu and the two Lords sat together and took Their meal,
so today take Your meal in my house — let these worthless eyes rejoice to see it."
All the mahantas agreed, saying, "Very well," and my Lord went to offer the food.
First He offered food to Sri Mahaprabhu, and on His right He placed Nityananda's offering;
on Gauranga's left the Lord Himself sat down. Seeing this, the Sri Vaishnavas raised the sound of Hari's name.
Master Virachandra performed the arati of the meal and, lighting incense and lamps, gazed upon the moonlike face.
With fresh love all the mahantas sang the kirtana of the arati of Gauranga's meal.
What that wondrous beauty was, the root of bliss, I cannot describe: my good fortune is small.
In the midst of the assembly Virabhadra raised his arms and said: "Hear one word of mine, all you Vaishnavas:
whoever holds a festival with a feast, let him likewise first offer food to the three Lords,
and afterwards carefully distribute that maha-prasada to sadhus, brahmanas and Vaishnavas.
By the meal of the three Lords the great sacrifice becomes complete; by the meal of the three Lords even the seat of honour is blessed.
Sri Chaitanya, Nityananda and Advaita Gosani — the three are one, and the one is three: They are not different.
Whoever sees a difference among the three will never attain the feet of Chaitanya.
Without Gaura's mercy one will not obtain loving devotion, and so rare a birth will pass in vain.
At whatever festival food is not offered to the three Lords, that person's sacrifice, like the sacrifice of Daksha, will not be completed.
He will not obtain the fruit of giving food: all will be ruined, the sacrifice will come to nothing,
and in the next world he will dwell in hell, and as long as the moon and sun shine he will find no release."
Hearing such words from Virachandra's lips, all the Vaishnavas said, "So be it! So be it!"
Then, after the meal, the Lord rose, rinsed His mouth and accepted betel.
Then Master Virabhadra joyfully distributed that maha-prasada.
All the brahmanas, Vaishnavas, sadhus, mahantas and others, receiving maha-prasada, felt their lives fulfilled.
After the festival Virachandra, receiving the Lord's order, joyfully prepared for the rite of offering (pashar).
In a new pot was curd mixed with turmeric, and on top fresh mango leaves made a lovely sight.
Covering it with a new cloth, he set it before Advaita.
At my Lord's order Sri Achyutananda performed the offering, joyfully singing kirtana.
Having performed the rite of auspicious curd (dadhi-mangala), all the associates of Sri Gauranga danced in the mood of the cowherds of Gokula.
The bliss that arose — I see no shore to it; for my own purification I write down only a particle of its essence.
After the festival the devotees went to their own places, and the Lord returned with us to Shantipura.
Back in His home the Lord was sorrowful: no other words were on His lips but "Hare Krishna."
One day I, a worm, at the Lord's order went to learn news of Navadvipa and came back to Shantipura.
I fell flat at the Lord's feet, and the Lord said, "Ishanadasa, tell the news."
I said: "The residents of Navadvipa are all deeply grieved at Gauranga's disappearance.
By good fortune I saw Damodara Pandita; he asked, 'Why have you come here?'
After Shachi-devi's disappearance Mother Vishnupriya, of her own will, had the devotees close the doors.
Without her permission no one may see her: she has taken upon herself an extremely severe vow.
At dawn, having bathed and performed the daily rites, she chants Hari's name, taking a little rice:
for each name she puts one grain of rice into a clay pot — thus she chants the name until the third watch of the day.
When her japa is finished, she takes only as many grains of rice as there were names, and carefully cooks them with her face covered by a cloth.
Without salt, without spices — she offers this rice to Mahaprabhu with pleading.
With many lamentations she gives water for rinsing the mouth, and she herself eats only a handful of the prasada.
The rest of the prasada she gives to the devotees. Who else could keep so severe a vow?'
Hearing these words, which fell like a thunderbolt, I thought: how can I have darshana of Mother?
At that time Gadadhara Dasa, Sri Rama Pandita and other eminent devotees came there.
All together with Damodara, to receive prasada, they entered the inner apartments with tears in their eyes.
Then, at Mother Vishnupriya's order, the Pandita took me, unworthy, into the inner apartments.
Going in, I saw that Mother's body was covered with a thick cloth; by the good fortune of millions of lives I saw only her holy feet.
By a particle of the devotees' mercy I received a little prasada: I felt my life fulfilled, and the sorrow left my heart.
What hardships Mother endures — what more can I say? Without superhuman power who could do such a thing?"
Hearing this, my Lord wept, but, accepting Krishna's will, He restrained His grief.
The state of Mother Vishnupriya that I saw with my own eyes — to tell it breaks my heart; I could not write it down.
Some days later Lord Sitanatha, sitting in the courtyard, was reading the Srimad-Bhagavatam.
At that time a pure Vaishnava came and bowed before the Lord with the eight limbs of his body.
The Lord asked him, "Where have you come from now?" He replied, "Lord, Virabhadra has sent me.
He is twenty years old, yet still uninitiated, for want of a worthy guru.
Therefore, hoping to receive mantra from You, he is coming here by boat, absorbed in prema."
The Lord said: "This decision of Vira's is not right: it goes against the consent of his own people.
Go and explain My words to Vira: let him receive mantra from Mother Jahnava."
Hearing this, the Sri Vaishnava went to Khardaha and conveyed the Lord's order to Jahnava.
Hearing it, Sri Jahnava sent a sadhu, brought Vira back and initiated him.
Now hear of the disappearance of Sri Advaita Prabhu — as I write of it, my heart breaks.
One day the Lord was seized by a great ecstasy and wandered about searching: "Where is Nimai?"
After a long while outer consciousness returned to the Acharya, and He called His beloved sons.
The Lord said: "Hear, My children, of My sorrow: wicked people of Mine blaspheme Gauranga.
My heart cannot bear this; in atonement for it I shall surely leave this body.
Therefore convey My order and bring here the dear devotees of Sri Gauranga."
Having said this, my Lord became motionless, and Sri Achyuta quickly sent the news everywhere.
Receiving the letter with the Lord's order, Master Virachandra came to Shantipura with the devotees.
From Ambika came Gauridasa Pandita; all the devotees of Navadvipa came to the Lord.
With his devotees came Sarkar Thakura; there came the best of panditas, Kavi Karnapura,
Shyamadasa, Vishnudasa, Sri Yadunandana and all the other beloved disciples of Advaita.
Arriving in Shantipura, all bowed at the Lord's feet with the eight limbs of their bodies and offered prayers.
The Lord said: "You are all most dear to Me. Faithfully carry out one word of Mine:
preach the qualities and the dharma of Sri Chaitanya Mahaprabhu as far as you are able — this is the core of My heart.
The company of all the unbelievers and boors who hate Sri Gauranga must certainly be abandoned.
And now all of you, singing kirtana to Gaura, fulfil the long-cherished desire of My heart."
Hearing this, all the devotees were filled with prema and began sankirtana of Gaura's name and qualities.
Sri Achyuta, Krishna Mishra, Gopala Thakura, Master Virachandra, Narahari full of rasa,
Gauridasa Pandita and Damodara Pandita — these seven danced most beautifully.
Hearing of Gaura's qualities, the Lord overflowed with prema, entered the sankirtana and began to dance.
The waves of the ocean of sankirtana rose ever higher, and Sri Advaita sank into them in mahabhava.
The jewels of trembling stupor and the other ecstatic symptoms adorned the Lord's whole body, and He wept: "Where is Gora, My life?"
The Lord's wondrous emotions are impossible for an ordinary soul; surrounding the Lord, all the devotees wept with prema.
Then the Lord said, "Here, I have found Gauranga!" — and His body became like a kadamba flower.
Suddenly He entered the holy temple of Madana-Gopala — and became invisible to ordinary people.
Looking for the Lord, the devotees ran here and there; not finding Him, they wept and rolled in the dust.
Sri Achyuta, understanding that Sri Advaita had disappeared, weeping aloud, said to all of Gaura's associates:
"Of the wish-fulfilling tree of love for Gaura one trunk remained — therefore Gaura's disappearance was not complete.
Today the pastimes of Gauranga have come to their close." Hearing this, all the devotees wept without ceasing.
"Ah, Gauranga! Ah, Gauranga! Ah, Nityananda! Glory to the avatara as devotee, Sri Advaitachandra!" —
apart from these words nothing was on anyone's lips; from that grief even stones truly melted.
A day and a night passed with no one in outer consciousness; on the second day all bathed in the Ganga.
Master Sri Achyuta held a great festival, and all, receiving maha-prasada, went to their own places.
One hundred and twenty-five years the Lord remained on earth and in due order manifested countless pastimes.
That ocean of the nectar of His pastimes is inaccessible and uncrossable: Ananta finds no end to it — what then of me, worthless as I am?
For my own purification I have dared to do this: I could not touch even one drop of the ocean of His pastimes.
I have neither learning nor intelligence — how should I write a book? What I wished to write and what I have written, dharma is witness.
(My sources are) the sutras on the childhood pastimes (written by) Laudiya Krishnadasa — by reading that book the world is purified;
what I read and what I heard from Krishnadasa's lips, what Padmanabha and Shyamadasa told me;
the pastimes I saw with my own sinful eyes — all this, at the Lord's order, I have woven into a book.
In the year 1490 of the Shaka era I completed this book of pastimes in holy Lauda.
Why I came to holy Lauda — this confidential truth I shall tell the saintly briefly.
One day the Lord said to me in private: "My heart can no longer bear separation from Gauranga.
Soon I shall become invisible to the world of the living. Proclaim unceasingly Gaura's name and Gaura's qualities.
And I will tell you one thing more — listen attentively: you are My beloved disciple, like My own son.
When I am no longer seen, do not grieve: preach Gaura's name in My native land.
Faithfully carry out this order of Mine." Having said this, the Lord fell silent.
I think: if the order of the guru is carried out, then my birth and deeds will surely be fruitful.
After the Lord's disappearance Sita Thakurani — I do not know with what thought — gave me this order:
"O Ishanadasa, I love you dearly; I shall be pleased if you marry."
I said: "Mother, consider what you are ordering: to carry out this order is beyond my power.
I am nearly seventy years old — what brahmana would give me his daughter?"
Mother replied: "Krishna always fulfils His devotees' desires — that is why He is called the wish-fulfilling tree of the devotees.
Go east with Sri Jagadananda: he will take care to arrange your marriage.
There preach Gaura's name and dharma: by that many souls will be delivered.
Your descendants will become great bhagavatas and, giving the name of Hari, will set souls free."
Taking this order of Mother Sita upon my head, I came with Jagadananda Raya to the eastern country.
To continue the line and carry out the Lord's order, I came in haste to holy Lauda.
Living here, I wrote this book: I have only carried out the order of my guru.
I have written down only the essence, as I was ordered: let neither fault nor merit in it rest on me.
This is the alms I beg of the Vaishnavas who hear it: out of your own goodness forgive the offences of me, the lowly.
I am very old and have no knowledge at all: this book I have dedicated to the feet of Sri Chaitanya.
What was within my power, that I have written; may the sadhus in their kindness correct it.
The feet of guru, Krishna and the Vaishnavas are the essence of all: to the feet of them all I offer millions of obeisances.
These three are one reality in different forms: to deliver souls they manifest many forms,
— as in an earring and a necklace different shapes are seen, yet the cause is one, gold, and the soul perceives it.
These three are the sources of the avataras, oceans of mercy: the feet of these three are my boat across the ocean of worldly existence.
This is my prayer at the feet of these three: I am a great offender; my offences cannot be counted.
Out of Your own goodness pardon my offences — show forth Your name "Purifier of the fallen."
In all the three worlds there is none as fallen as I: may I at the end obtain a place at the reddish holy feet.

advaita-prakasha.title: Сон Адвайты: Гаура и Нитьянанда родятся сыновьями Кришна Мишры — Рагхунатха и Долаговинда
advaita-prakasha.summary: Махапрабху во сне говорит Адвайте: «Нада, не печалься: ты увидишь Меня в сыне Кришнамишры, а Нитьянанду — в его втором сыне»; в тот же день у Кришна Мишры рождается Рагхунатха, подобие Гауранги, а в полнолуние праздника качелей — Долаговинда, подобие Нитьянанды.

verses.text: С того дня Господь, великий владыка йоги, непрестанно медитировал на облик Шри Гауранги.
Во сне к Адвайте пришёл Махапрабху и сказал: «Нада, не печалься в сердце о разлуке со Мной.
Притянутый твоей любовью, Я пришёл в твой дом: ты увидишь Меня в облике сына Кришнамишры.
А Господа Нитьянанду-чанда через несколько дней обретёшь в своём доме в облике (второго) сына Кришнамишры.
Твой любимый как жизнь сын Кришнадас — в его сердце Я всегда играю.
Это Мой вечный преданный, поставленный на служение; чтобы исполнить его желание, Я снова явлюсь».
Увидев этот удивительный сон, Господь изумился — и в тот же день у Кришнамишры родился сын.
Он был подобием Шри Гауранги, чаровал мир; увидев его облик, Господь погрузился в любовь.
Звали его Рагхунатха; он был рудником любви и, слыша о достоинствах Гауры, проливал слёзы.
Затем в должное время, в полнолуние праздника качелей Кришны, у Кришнамишры родился второй сын —
подобие Нитьянанды, океан милости, непрестанно говоривший о величии Гауранги.
Господь дал ему имя Шри Долагови́нда; услышав это, преданные в любви восклицали имя Хари.

verses_en.text: Glory, glory to Sri Chaitanya! Glory to Sitanatha! Glory to Nityananda-Rama together with the devotees!
One day Mahaprabhu, sitting in seclusion, said to His most beloved Sri Jagadananda:
"Go quickly to the land of Gauda; first go to Nadia, the place where I was born.
Convey to My mother's feet My millions of obeisances: wherever I may be, I am her servant.
Being a son, I have not been able to fulfil a son's duty, and therefore I am a great offender at her feet.
Even in millions of yugas I cannot repay My debt to her — unless she forgives My offence by her nectarean mercy.
Then I shall be saved; otherwise I shall fall. I take shelter at her holy lotus feet.
Convey My message to the devotees of Krishna, and especially tell the Acharya."
Receiving Mahaprabhu's command, Sri Jagadananda bowed to Gaurachandra and set out for Gauda.
In due course he arrived in Navadvipa and, coming to the feet of Mother Shachi, prostrated himself.
He conveyed the humble words of Sri Gauranga, and hearing them, Shachi blessed Him again and again.
Sri Jagadananda, the necklace on the neck of Gaura's devotees, served Mother Shachi in many ways.
He gave the devotees the news of Sri Gauranga, and hearing it, the pure devotees became mad with love.
Some said: "Ah, Gauranga, why did You become a sannyasi? Having given us the shade of Your feet, why have You plunged us into grief?"
Others said: "My great good fortune has dawned: out of mercy Gora, my life, has remembered me."
Saddened by the devotees' grief, the pandit went to Shantipura and bowed at the Lord's feet.
The Lord embraced him tightly with love and quickly gave him the best seat.
Filled with love, He asked about Gauranga's welfare, and the pandit told in detail the truth about Gaura:
"Now Sri Krishna Chaitanya is always in the divine madness of love: now, crying 'Radha, Radha!', He grieves,
now with a roar He calls: 'Where is the Lord of My life?' — at that cry the heart of every living being melts."
Hearing this, my Lord became mad with pure love: "Ah, Lord!" — without Gauranga He had no other words.
After a watch the Lord became stunned, and in the second watch He roared loudly.
Now He laughed loudly, now He wept, uttering only: "Appearance and disappearance."
Thus many moods arose in Him — I, unworthy, have no power to describe them.
What I see, that I write, not understanding the meaning — as a parrot sings a song because it has been taught.
Then the Lord honoured the pandit lavishly, and they spent the night talking of Gaura's qualities.
In the morning Jagadananda humbly asked Sri Advaita's leave to go.
The Lord spoke in hints a riddle (tarja) which no one but Gaura can understand.
The Lord said: "Sri Gauranga is the treasure of My life. Convey this to His crimson holy feet:
tell the Baul: 'People have become bauls (madmen)'; tell the Baul: 'Rice no longer sells in the market';
tell the Baul: 'There is no more need for the work'; tell the Baul: 'This is said by a baul.'"
Hearing this, Sri Jagadananda smiled slightly and, having pleased the Lord, set out for Nilachala.
After some days he arrived at Sri Kshetra; seeing Gaura, he shed streams of love from both eyes.
He prostrated himself before Sri Chaitanya with the eight limbs of his body, and He rose and embraced Sri Jagadananda.
Then, joining his palms, the pandit related in order: "The devotees of Nadia are well.
Incomparable is the motherly love of Mother Shachi: for Your welfare she prays to the gods.
She begs blessings for You from the sadhus and, raising her arms, blesses You herself.
What more can I say of Mother Vishnupriya? Seeing her devotion and fidelity, I was amazed.
She serves Mother Shachi in many ways — a thousand people could not serve like that.
Every day at dawn she goes with Mother Shachi to bathe in the Ganga and returns home.
And after that, until the end of the day, she never goes out: neither moon nor sun sees her face.
All the devotees who come for prasada see only her holy feet, not her face.
No one can hear her voice; the lotus of her face is always withered, and tears flow from her eyes.
Eating only the remnants on Mother Shachi's plate, she maintains her body only for the sake of service.
When she has time from serving Shachi, she sits in seclusion and ceaselessly chants the Name.
She has a great taste for the nectar of the name of Hari; the crown of chaste women, her body is full of pure love.
Her faith in Your holy feet is deep; by her mercy I came to know her.
She has made a portrait exactly like Your form and consecrated it with the great mantra of loving devotion.
That murti she serves secretly and diligently, having surrendered herself to Your lotus feet.
Even Sri Ananta cannot enumerate her good qualities — how much can I tell You with a single mouth?"
Mahaprabhu said: "Speak no more of this. Give Me the news from the Acharya of Shantipura."
First the pandit told of the Lord's (Advaita's) welfare, and then he delivered His riddle.
Hearing the riddle, Sri Chaitanya said with a smile: "As He permits, so do I accept."
Having said this, Gauranga became stunned, and Svarupa and the other devotees asked Him:
"Tell us, Mahaprabhu, what is the meaning of this riddle? None of us can understand it."
Sri Gauranga said: "This is Advaita Acharya: He has done an unearthly deed — He has made Krishna manifest.
Bhagavan Himself is bound by the rope of His love: by His will Krishna appears and disappears.
Who can understand the meaning of His riddle? He alone understands its meaning; it is not revealed to others."
The sadhus call Him the honoured one among the gods: He is the wish-fulfilling tree of devotion, worshipped by the world.
Hearing this, the devotees were amazed at heart. From that day a change came over Gora.
The divine madness of Sri Radha awoke in Him: "Ah, Lord! Ah, Krishna!" He wept.
In the ecstasy of mahabhava He did not distinguish day from night, and fear settled in the hearts of the devotees.
One day Gora, gazing at Jagannatha, entered the holy temple with the words "Ah, Lord!"
As soon as He entered, the doors closed by themselves, and grave fears arose in the hearts of the devotees.
After some time the doors opened by themselves, and all understood that Gauranga had disappeared.
Although for the devotees Chaitanya has not disappeared, Gaura's companions, following the custom of the world, expressed great grief.
That grief, like the fire of Rudra, of great intensity, burnt the bodies, minds and lives of all beings.
The pastimes of Sri Gauranga are a boundless ocean: Ananta cannot describe even one stream of it.
I am more insignificant than the most insignificant worm: in the bliss of consciousness I tell only a speck of the essence.
Meanwhile my Lord, in an unearthly ecstasy, understood in His heart that Mahaprabhu had disappeared.
The Lord fell into divine madness, lost external awareness and called: "Nimai! Nimai!"
Now He said: "Come here, Nimai, take your books: there is housework — I must go quickly to teach."
Now He said: "I know all Your tricks: tell Me, in what mood did You become Gaura?"
Now He said: "Nimai, stay in My house: if you go to foreign lands, Mother Shachi will grieve."
Now He said: "Gaura, You are the creator of the creator: in the age of Kali You have become the father of the sankirtana of the Name."
And sometimes He said: "You have hidden the treasure of Vraja in Vraja; I search and cannot find it. What tricks are You playing?"
Thus He said aloud many incoherent things; after a long time the Lord's external awareness returned.
Crying "Hari, Hari!", He roared, and all said: "Now the ailment has passed."
Who can understand this pure mahabhava? Only the pure devotees understand it in their hearts.
I, the most insignificant worm, have not a shadow of knowledge: what I saw, its essence I have revealed.
One day Sitanatha, sitting at the gate, was joyfully crying out the names "Hare Krishna."
A devotee who lived in Kshetra came there; seeing him, the Lord seated him respectfully.
Following worldly custom, He, shedding tears, asked very anxiously about Gauranga's welfare.
The Sri Vaishnava said: "I know the news of Chaitanya: the report is that He has disappeared."
Hearing this, the Lord saw everything become empty and, saying "I understood! I understood!", fainted.
After a long time He came to Himself; how many moods appeared in the Lord cannot be described.
Now stupor, now a roar, now rolling on the ground, now with cries of "Gora! Gora!" He wept aloud.
Hearing the weeping, Mother Sita came there; learning the reason, she fainted.
After a long time Sita-devi came to herself and wept loudly, repeating: "Chaitanya!"
Sri Achyuta wept, Krishnadasa wept, Sri Gopaladasa wept, in despair.
Among Sita's sons these three are foremost: they are pure devotees, the lives of the three are given to Gaura.
I have no power to describe their weeping: I have described only a speck of the essence.
A day and a night passed, and the Lord had no external awareness; the Acharya with all His family fasted.
The next day the Lord held a great festival: many brahmanas and Sri Vaishnavas were fed.
Hundreds of poor people received food, and mountains of clothes and cowries were distributed.
In the nectar of the sankirtana of Hari, in the pure waters of the Ganga, Shantipura floated away into the ocean of love.
In its waves many villagers with their families bathed and were immersed.
From that day the Lord, the great master of yoga, ceaselessly meditated on the form of Sri Gauranga.
In a dream Mahaprabhu came to Advaita and said: "Nada, do not grieve in your heart over separation from Me.
Drawn by your love, I have come to your house: you will see Me in the form of Krishna Mishra's son.
And Lord Nityananda-chandra you will find in your house after some days in the form of (another) son of Krishna Mishra.
Your son Krishnadasa, dear to you as life — in his heart I always sport.
He is My eternal devotee, appointed to service; to fulfil his desire I shall appear again."
Having seen this wonderful dream, the Lord was amazed — and on that very day a son was born to Krishna Mishra.
He was the likeness of Sri Gauranga, enchanting the world; seeing his form, the Lord was immersed in love.
His name was Raghunatha; he was a mine of love and, hearing of Gaura's qualities, shed tears.
Then in due time, on the full moon of Krishna's swing festival, a second son was born to Krishna Mishra —
the likeness of Nityananda, an ocean of mercy, who ceaselessly spoke of the glory of Gauranga.
The Lord gave him the name Sri Dolagovinda; hearing it, the devotees cried out the name of Hari in love.
One day Sri Advaita called His sons together and in seclusion spoke to them very gently:
"O children! Calm your minds, all of you, and hear the essence of the dharma of the householder.
Whoever daily performs the sandhya worship and the five great sacrifices is a great sage.
Do not covet another's wife or another's wealth — for that you will suffer both in this world and in the next.
Be merciful to all beings, do no harm; do not blaspheme the sadhus, but praise them.
Plant Sri Tulasi in the courtyard of your house: a house without tulasi is like a cremation ground.
The daily sankirtana of Hari is best of all: it is the atonement for sins, before it Yama himself flees.
Daily association with saints destroys offences; devotion to Krishna is obtained, there is no doubt.
And remember one more word of Mine: do nothing for your own pleasure.
If one leads a householder's life for the service of Krishna, one does not partake of the sin or merit born of deeds.
From selfish deeds worldly desires gradually grow, and by that thread the soul is bound to coming and going in the world.
Therefore give up selfish deeds altogether: if you act for Krishna's sake, your desires will be fulfilled."
Thus He gave many kinds of instruction, and hearing them, Sri Achyuta and the others rejoiced.
Sri Achyuta, Krishna Mishra and Gopaladasa — these three always have jubilation in the service of Krishna.
They always have deep love for Krishna and the Vaishnavas, and Sri Achyuta has complete detachment from the world.
At the Lord's command the waves of the Ganga of love rose, and they began the service of Krishna with various offerings.
Although the minds of all three were wholly given to Krishna, the Lord resolved to entrust the service to Krishna Mishra.
The householder Sri Krishna Mishra is full of pure devotion — the Lord considered him worthy of the service of Krishna.
The son of Labha said to Achyuta: "Listen, My son Sri Achyuta, to My word.
You are My eldest son, the foremost of Vaishnavas: having obtained such a son, I am blessed.
You are supremely pure, in the shastras a Brihaspati, the crown of the righteous, with a most pure mind.
From childhood you have been detached from the world, always devoted to the dharma of supreme detachment.
Therefore you turned away from marriage and considered paltry the pleasures of the external senses so dear to souls.
Therefore I have understood: the service of the Deity and the rites are not your way.
Krishnadasa Mishra, your younger brother, devoted to the gods and brahmanas, the best of Vaishnavas,
most learned, pure of mind, keeper of the treasures of devotion, the crown of lovers, always pure in conduct,
accepts My view and is always obedient to Me; his life is given to Gaura — therefore he is dear to Gaura.
Having married, he has become a householder: in My view he is worthy of the service of Krishna.
All the more since Krishnadasa has two sons — supremely righteous, devoted to Sri Gauranga.
The elder is Raghunatha, the younger Sri Dolagovinda: both find supreme bliss in the service of Sri Krishna.
One day Sriman Raghunatha said to Me: 'How will the word of Veda-Vyasa come true?
(It is said that) in the age of Kali the eighty-four hells will be filled; but Sri Krishna Chaitanya has closed that road —
by the great mantra of the name of Hari He has delivered the souls. Tell me: how will the hells be filled?'
Hearing this, Sri Dolagovinda laughed and said: 'They will be filled with all the sinners who hate Gaura.'
Hearing such words, I was amazed, and since then I know that both are incarnations of gods.
Blessed is My Krishnadasa, blessed are his sons: they are worthy of the service of Sri Madana-Gopala.
He is My own who worships Gauranga: he is fit to serve the treasure of My life.
Therefore I wish to entrust this service to Krishna Mishra. What is your wish?"
Hearing this, Sri Achyuta joyfully said, joining his palms: "As You have commanded, so I too think."
Then Sri Advaita said to Krishna Mishra: "Madana-Gopala is the Lord of My life.
Serve Him with devotion every day; do not allow those turned away from Him to worship Him.
Know that the averse are unbelievers, heretics, Advaitin sannyasis, yogis and jnanis,
those desiring enjoyment and liberation, devoid of the desire for devotion: these non-Vaishnavas I regard as averse to Krishna.
Among Vaishnavas, one who is outside a sampradaya, and among those of a sampradaya, one who does not acknowledge Gauranga —
he is surely averse to Krishna — this I shall determine. And one more word of Mine, listen, Krishnadasa:
those of My own who are evil-minded, who, transgressing My command, go their own way and do not acknowledge Gora —
(know:) Sri Gauranga is My Lord, I am His servant, the dust of His holy feet is My food.
Gora is the Lord of My life, Gora is the One I worship: whoever does not acknowledge that Gauranga is rejected by Me.
Those averse to Krishna are all in a low refuge: they are never fit to serve the Deity (sri-vigraha) of Krishna.
Whoever preserves the true dharma of his father is the real son — such is the word of the Vedas."
Having said this, He insistently entrusted the Deity of Sri Madana-Gopala to Krishna Mishra.
Having received the service of Krishna, Krishna Mishra in the bliss of love prostrated himself at the Lord's lotus feet.
With humble praise he bowed at his mother's feet, and Sita and Advaita both blessed him.
Then he humbly bowed to Sri Achyuta; Achyuta said: "I offer myself to your good fortune.
Krishna wished to show you mercy and revealed that wish through His own devotee,
as Krishna revealed the Vedas through Brahma" — and having said this, he embraced Krishna Mishra.
Gopala said: "Krishna is most merciful: by His mercy He will bring good to the whole family,
as when one waters the root of a tree, the branches, leaves and the rest are filled with joy."
"What good fortune!" — having said this, he bowed to Krishna Mishra, and Krishna Mishra embraced him tightly.
But the Acharya's other sons — Master Balarama and the very mighty Master Jagadisha —
in anger, after consulting with their people, diligently procured another Deity of Krishna,
performed the bathing ceremony and installed that Deity, and held a festival with their own people.
The pastimes of Sri Advaita are an impassable ocean: I have proclaimed only a drop of their essence.
Placing his hope in the feet of Sri Chaitanya and Sri Advaita, Ishana Nagara tells the Advaita-prakasha.

advaita-prakasha.title: Наставление Адвайты сыновьям о дхарме домохозяина; служение Мадана-Гопале вверено Кришна Мишре
advaita-prakasha.summary: Адвайта учит сыновей: сандхья и пять жертвоприношений, милость ко всем, туласи во дворе, ежедневная санкиртана, общение со святыми и жизнь ради служения Кришне; отрешённому Ачьюте служение Божеству не по пути, и Адвайта вверяет Мадана-Гопалу домохозяину Кришна Мишре, отцу Рагхунатхи и Долаговинды, запрещая допускать к служению отвернувшихся — в том числе тех, кто не признаёт Гаурангу; Ачьюта и Гопала радуются, а Баларама и Джагадиша в гневе устанавливают другое Божество Кришны.

verses.text: Однажды Шри Адвайта созвал сыновей и в уединении очень ласково сказал:
«О дети! Успокойте все ум и выслушайте суть дхармы домохозяина.
Кто ежедневно совершает сандхья-вандану и пять великих жертвоприношений, тот — великий мудрец.
Не желайте чужой жены и чужого богатства — за это будете мучиться и в этом мире, и в ином.
Будьте милостивы ко всем существам, не причиняйте вреда; не хулите, а хвалите садху.
Во дворе дома сажайте Шри Туласи: дом без туласи подобен месту сожжения.
Ежедневная санкиртана Хари — лучше всего: это искупление грехов, от него бежит сам Яма.
Ежедневное общение со святыми уничтожает оскорбления; обретается преданность Кришне, нет сомнения.
И ещё одно Моё слово помните: ничего не делайте ради собственного удовольствия.
Если вести домашнюю жизнь ради служения Кришне, не станешь причастным ни греху, ни заслуге от деяний.
От корыстных деяний постепенно растут мирские желания, и этой нитью душа связана с приходами и уходами в мире.
Поэтому совершенно оставьте корыстные деяния: если действовать ради Кришны, исполнятся желания».
Так Он дал многоразличные наставления, и, слушая, Шри Ачьюта и другие возрадовались.
Шри Ачьюта, Кришнамишра и Гопаладас — у этих троих всегдашнее ликование в служении Кришне.
У них всегда глубокая любовь к Кришне и вайшнавам, а у Шри Ачьюты — полная отрешённость от мира.
По повелению Господа поднялись волны Ганги любви, и они начали служение Кришне с разными подношениями.
Хотя ум всех троих был всецело отдан Кришне, Господь решил вверить служение Кришнамишре.
Домохозяин Шри Кришнамишра исполнен чистой преданности — Господь счёл его достойным служения Кришне.
Сын Лабхи сказал Ачьюте: «Послушай, сынок Шри Ачьюта, Моё слово.
Ты — Мой старший сын, первый среди вайшнавов: получив такого сына, Я благословен.
Ты в высшей степени чист, в шастрах ты — Брихаспати, венец праведных, с чистейшим разумом.
С детства ты отрешён от мира, всегда предан дхарме высшей отрешённости.
Поэтому ты отвернулся от брака и счёл ничтожными удовольствия внешних чувств, любезные душам.
Поэтому Я понял: служение Божеству и обряды тебе не по пути.
Кришнадас Мишра — твой младший брат, преданный богам и брахманам, лучший из вайшнавов,
весьма учёный, чистый умом, хранитель сокровищ преданности, венец любящих, всегда чистый в поведении.
Он принимает Мой взгляд, всегда Мне послушен; его жизнь отдана Гауре — потому он и любезен Гауре.
Женившись, он стал домохозяином: по Моему мнению, он достоин служения Кришне.
Тем более что у Кришнадаса два сына — в высшей степени праведные, преданные Шри Гауранге.
Старший — Рагхунатха, младший — Шри Долаговинда: оба находят высшее блаженство в служении Шри Кришне.
Однажды Шриман Рагхунатха сказал Мне: „Как же сбудется слово Веда-Вьясы?
(Сказано, что) в век Кали восемьдесят четыре ада будут переполнены; а Шри Кришна Чайтанья закрыл этот путь —
великой мантрой имени Хари Он спас души. Скажи: как же наполнятся ады?“
Услышав это, Шри Долаговинда, смеясь, сказал: „Они наполнятся всеми грешниками, ненавидящими Гауру“.
Услышав такие слова, Я изумился и с тех пор знаю, что оба — воплощения богов.
Благословен Мой Кришнадас, благословенны его сыновья: они достойны служения Шри Мадана-Гопале.
Тот Мне родной, кто поклоняется Гауранге: он и достоин служить сокровищу Моей жизни.
Поэтому Я хочу вверить это служение Кришнамишре. Каково твоё желание?»
Услышав это, Шри Ачьюта радостно сказал, сложив ладони: «Как Ты повелел, так и я думаю».
Тогда Шри Адвайта сказал Кришнамишре: «Мадана-Гопала — Владыка Моей жизни.
С преданностью служи Ему каждый день; не давай поклоняться Ему тем, кто отвернулся от Него.
Знай: отвернувшиеся — это неверующие, безбожники, санньяси-адвайтисты, йоги и гьяни,
жаждущие наслаждения и освобождения, лишённые желания преданности: их, невайшнавов, Я считаю отвернувшимися от Кришны.
Среди вайшнавов — тот, кто вне сампрадаи, а среди принадлежащих к сампрадае — тот, кто не признаёт Гаурангу:
он, несомненно, отвернулся от Кришны, — вот что Я определю. И ещё одно Моё слово, послушай, Кришнадас:
те из Моих, кто злонамерен, кто, нарушив Моё повеление, идёт своим путём и не признаёт Гору, —
(знай:) Шри Гауранга — Мой Господь, Я — Его слуга, пыль Его святых стоп — Моя пища.
Гора — Владыка Моей жизни, Гора — Тот, кому Я поклоняюсь: кто не признаёт этого Гаурангу, тот Мною отвергнут.
Отвернувшиеся от Кришны — все они в низком прибежище: они никогда не достойны служить Божеству (шри-виграхе) Кришны.
Кто сохраняет праведную дхарму отца, тот и есть истинный сын — таково слово Вед».
Сказав так, Он настойчиво вверил Божество Шри Мадана-Гопалы Кришнамишре.
Получив служение Кришне, Кришнамишра в блаженстве любви простёрся у лотосных стоп Господа.
Со смиренной хвалой он поклонился стопам матери, и Сита и Адвайта оба благословили его.
Затем он смиренно поклонился Шри Ачьюте; Ачьюта сказал: «Я отдаю себя твоей удаче.
Кришна пожелал явить тебе милость и проявил это желание через Своего преданного,
как Кришна явил Веды через Брахму», — и, сказав так, обнял Кришнамишру.
Гопала сказал: «Кришна весьма милостив: по милости Он принесёт благо всему роду,
как если поливать корень дерева, то ветви, листья и прочее наполняются радостью».
«Какая удача!» — сказав так, он поклонился Кришнамишре, а Кришнамишра крепко его обнял.
Но другие сыновья Ачарьи — Господин Баларама и весьма могучий Господин Джагадиша —
в гневе, посовещавшись со своими людьми, с усердием раздобыли другое Божество Кришны,
совершили омовение и установили это Божество, а со своими людьми устроили праздник.
Игры Шри Адвайты — неодолимый океан: я возвестил лишь каплю их сути.
Уповая на стопы Шри Чайтаньи и Шри Адвайты, Ишана Нагара повествует «Адвайта-пракашу».

verses_en.text: Glory, glory to Sri Chaitanya! Glory to Sitanatha! Glory to Nityananda-Rama together with the devotees!
One day Mahaprabhu, sitting in seclusion, said to His most beloved Sri Jagadananda:
"Go quickly to the land of Gauda; first go to Nadia, the place where I was born.
Convey to My mother's feet My millions of obeisances: wherever I may be, I am her servant.
Being a son, I have not been able to fulfil a son's duty, and therefore I am a great offender at her feet.
Even in millions of yugas I cannot repay My debt to her — unless she forgives My offence by her nectarean mercy.
Then I shall be saved; otherwise I shall fall. I take shelter at her holy lotus feet.
Convey My message to the devotees of Krishna, and especially tell the Acharya."
Receiving Mahaprabhu's command, Sri Jagadananda bowed to Gaurachandra and set out for Gauda.
In due course he arrived in Navadvipa and, coming to the feet of Mother Shachi, prostrated himself.
He conveyed the humble words of Sri Gauranga, and hearing them, Shachi blessed Him again and again.
Sri Jagadananda, the necklace on the neck of Gaura's devotees, served Mother Shachi in many ways.
He gave the devotees the news of Sri Gauranga, and hearing it, the pure devotees became mad with love.
Some said: "Ah, Gauranga, why did You become a sannyasi? Having given us the shade of Your feet, why have You plunged us into grief?"
Others said: "My great good fortune has dawned: out of mercy Gora, my life, has remembered me."
Saddened by the devotees' grief, the pandit went to Shantipura and bowed at the Lord's feet.
The Lord embraced him tightly with love and quickly gave him the best seat.
Filled with love, He asked about Gauranga's welfare, and the pandit told in detail the truth about Gaura:
"Now Sri Krishna Chaitanya is always in the divine madness of love: now, crying 'Radha, Radha!', He grieves,
now with a roar He calls: 'Where is the Lord of My life?' — at that cry the heart of every living being melts."
Hearing this, my Lord became mad with pure love: "Ah, Lord!" — without Gauranga He had no other words.
After a watch the Lord became stunned, and in the second watch He roared loudly.
Now He laughed loudly, now He wept, uttering only: "Appearance and disappearance."
Thus many moods arose in Him — I, unworthy, have no power to describe them.
What I see, that I write, not understanding the meaning — as a parrot sings a song because it has been taught.
Then the Lord honoured the pandit lavishly, and they spent the night talking of Gaura's qualities.
In the morning Jagadananda humbly asked Sri Advaita's leave to go.
The Lord spoke in hints a riddle (tarja) which no one but Gaura can understand.
The Lord said: "Sri Gauranga is the treasure of My life. Convey this to His crimson holy feet:
tell the Baul: 'People have become bauls (madmen)'; tell the Baul: 'Rice no longer sells in the market';
tell the Baul: 'There is no more need for the work'; tell the Baul: 'This is said by a baul.'"
Hearing this, Sri Jagadananda smiled slightly and, having pleased the Lord, set out for Nilachala.
After some days he arrived at Sri Kshetra; seeing Gaura, he shed streams of love from both eyes.
He prostrated himself before Sri Chaitanya with the eight limbs of his body, and He rose and embraced Sri Jagadananda.
Then, joining his palms, the pandit related in order: "The devotees of Nadia are well.
Incomparable is the motherly love of Mother Shachi: for Your welfare she prays to the gods.
She begs blessings for You from the sadhus and, raising her arms, blesses You herself.
What more can I say of Mother Vishnupriya? Seeing her devotion and fidelity, I was amazed.
She serves Mother Shachi in many ways — a thousand people could not serve like that.
Every day at dawn she goes with Mother Shachi to bathe in the Ganga and returns home.
And after that, until the end of the day, she never goes out: neither moon nor sun sees her face.
All the devotees who come for prasada see only her holy feet, not her face.
No one can hear her voice; the lotus of her face is always withered, and tears flow from her eyes.
Eating only the remnants on Mother Shachi's plate, she maintains her body only for the sake of service.
When she has time from serving Shachi, she sits in seclusion and ceaselessly chants the Name.
She has a great taste for the nectar of the name of Hari; the crown of chaste women, her body is full of pure love.
Her faith in Your holy feet is deep; by her mercy I came to know her.
She has made a portrait exactly like Your form and consecrated it with the great mantra of loving devotion.
That murti she serves secretly and diligently, having surrendered herself to Your lotus feet.
Even Sri Ananta cannot enumerate her good qualities — how much can I tell You with a single mouth?"
Mahaprabhu said: "Speak no more of this. Give Me the news from the Acharya of Shantipura."
First the pandit told of the Lord's (Advaita's) welfare, and then he delivered His riddle.
Hearing the riddle, Sri Chaitanya said with a smile: "As He permits, so do I accept."
Having said this, Gauranga became stunned, and Svarupa and the other devotees asked Him:
"Tell us, Mahaprabhu, what is the meaning of this riddle? None of us can understand it."
Sri Gauranga said: "This is Advaita Acharya: He has done an unearthly deed — He has made Krishna manifest.
Bhagavan Himself is bound by the rope of His love: by His will Krishna appears and disappears.
Who can understand the meaning of His riddle? He alone understands its meaning; it is not revealed to others."
The sadhus call Him the honoured one among the gods: He is the wish-fulfilling tree of devotion, worshipped by the world.
Hearing this, the devotees were amazed at heart. From that day a change came over Gora.
The divine madness of Sri Radha awoke in Him: "Ah, Lord! Ah, Krishna!" He wept.
In the ecstasy of mahabhava He did not distinguish day from night, and fear settled in the hearts of the devotees.
One day Gora, gazing at Jagannatha, entered the holy temple with the words "Ah, Lord!"
As soon as He entered, the doors closed by themselves, and grave fears arose in the hearts of the devotees.
After some time the doors opened by themselves, and all understood that Gauranga had disappeared.
Although for the devotees Chaitanya has not disappeared, Gaura's companions, following the custom of the world, expressed great grief.
That grief, like the fire of Rudra, of great intensity, burnt the bodies, minds and lives of all beings.
The pastimes of Sri Gauranga are a boundless ocean: Ananta cannot describe even one stream of it.
I am more insignificant than the most insignificant worm: in the bliss of consciousness I tell only a speck of the essence.
Meanwhile my Lord, in an unearthly ecstasy, understood in His heart that Mahaprabhu had disappeared.
The Lord fell into divine madness, lost external awareness and called: "Nimai! Nimai!"
Now He said: "Come here, Nimai, take your books: there is housework — I must go quickly to teach."
Now He said: "I know all Your tricks: tell Me, in what mood did You become Gaura?"
Now He said: "Nimai, stay in My house: if you go to foreign lands, Mother Shachi will grieve."
Now He said: "Gaura, You are the creator of the creator: in the age of Kali You have become the father of the sankirtana of the Name."
And sometimes He said: "You have hidden the treasure of Vraja in Vraja; I search and cannot find it. What tricks are You playing?"
Thus He said aloud many incoherent things; after a long time the Lord's external awareness returned.
Crying "Hari, Hari!", He roared, and all said: "Now the ailment has passed."
Who can understand this pure mahabhava? Only the pure devotees understand it in their hearts.
I, the most insignificant worm, have not a shadow of knowledge: what I saw, its essence I have revealed.
One day Sitanatha, sitting at the gate, was joyfully crying out the names "Hare Krishna."
A devotee who lived in Kshetra came there; seeing him, the Lord seated him respectfully.
Following worldly custom, He, shedding tears, asked very anxiously about Gauranga's welfare.
The Sri Vaishnava said: "I know the news of Chaitanya: the report is that He has disappeared."
Hearing this, the Lord saw everything become empty and, saying "I understood! I understood!", fainted.
After a long time He came to Himself; how many moods appeared in the Lord cannot be described.
Now stupor, now a roar, now rolling on the ground, now with cries of "Gora! Gora!" He wept aloud.
Hearing the weeping, Mother Sita came there; learning the reason, she fainted.
After a long time Sita-devi came to herself and wept loudly, repeating: "Chaitanya!"
Sri Achyuta wept, Krishnadasa wept, Sri Gopaladasa wept, in despair.
Among Sita's sons these three are foremost: they are pure devotees, the lives of the three are given to Gaura.
I have no power to describe their weeping: I have described only a speck of the essence.
A day and a night passed, and the Lord had no external awareness; the Acharya with all His family fasted.
The next day the Lord held a great festival: many brahmanas and Sri Vaishnavas were fed.
Hundreds of poor people received food, and mountains of clothes and cowries were distributed.
In the nectar of the sankirtana of Hari, in the pure waters of the Ganga, Shantipura floated away into the ocean of love.
In its waves many villagers with their families bathed and were immersed.
From that day the Lord, the great master of yoga, ceaselessly meditated on the form of Sri Gauranga.
In a dream Mahaprabhu came to Advaita and said: "Nada, do not grieve in your heart over separation from Me.
Drawn by your love, I have come to your house: you will see Me in the form of Krishna Mishra's son.
And Lord Nityananda-chandra you will find in your house after some days in the form of (another) son of Krishna Mishra.
Your son Krishnadasa, dear to you as life — in his heart I always sport.
He is My eternal devotee, appointed to service; to fulfil his desire I shall appear again."
Having seen this wonderful dream, the Lord was amazed — and on that very day a son was born to Krishna Mishra.
He was the likeness of Sri Gauranga, enchanting the world; seeing his form, the Lord was immersed in love.
His name was Raghunatha; he was a mine of love and, hearing of Gaura's qualities, shed tears.
Then in due time, on the full moon of Krishna's swing festival, a second son was born to Krishna Mishra —
the likeness of Nityananda, an ocean of mercy, who ceaselessly spoke of the glory of Gauranga.
The Lord gave him the name Sri Dolagovinda; hearing it, the devotees cried out the name of Hari in love.
One day Sri Advaita called His sons together and in seclusion spoke to them very gently:
"O children! Calm your minds, all of you, and hear the essence of the dharma of the householder.
Whoever daily performs the sandhya worship and the five great sacrifices is a great sage.
Do not covet another's wife or another's wealth — for that you will suffer both in this world and in the next.
Be merciful to all beings, do no harm; do not blaspheme the sadhus, but praise them.
Plant Sri Tulasi in the courtyard of your house: a house without tulasi is like a cremation ground.
The daily sankirtana of Hari is best of all: it is the atonement for sins, before it Yama himself flees.
Daily association with saints destroys offences; devotion to Krishna is obtained, there is no doubt.
And remember one more word of Mine: do nothing for your own pleasure.
If one leads a householder's life for the service of Krishna, one does not partake of the sin or merit born of deeds.
From selfish deeds worldly desires gradually grow, and by that thread the soul is bound to coming and going in the world.
Therefore give up selfish deeds altogether: if you act for Krishna's sake, your desires will be fulfilled."
Thus He gave many kinds of instruction, and hearing them, Sri Achyuta and the others rejoiced.
Sri Achyuta, Krishna Mishra and Gopaladasa — these three always have jubilation in the service of Krishna.
They always have deep love for Krishna and the Vaishnavas, and Sri Achyuta has complete detachment from the world.
At the Lord's command the waves of the Ganga of love rose, and they began the service of Krishna with various offerings.
Although the minds of all three were wholly given to Krishna, the Lord resolved to entrust the service to Krishna Mishra.
The householder Sri Krishna Mishra is full of pure devotion — the Lord considered him worthy of the service of Krishna.
The son of Labha said to Achyuta: "Listen, My son Sri Achyuta, to My word.
You are My eldest son, the foremost of Vaishnavas: having obtained such a son, I am blessed.
You are supremely pure, in the shastras a Brihaspati, the crown of the righteous, with a most pure mind.
From childhood you have been detached from the world, always devoted to the dharma of supreme detachment.
Therefore you turned away from marriage and considered paltry the pleasures of the external senses so dear to souls.
Therefore I have understood: the service of the Deity and the rites are not your way.
Krishnadasa Mishra, your younger brother, devoted to the gods and brahmanas, the best of Vaishnavas,
most learned, pure of mind, keeper of the treasures of devotion, the crown of lovers, always pure in conduct,
accepts My view and is always obedient to Me; his life is given to Gaura — therefore he is dear to Gaura.
Having married, he has become a householder: in My view he is worthy of the service of Krishna.
All the more since Krishnadasa has two sons — supremely righteous, devoted to Sri Gauranga.
The elder is Raghunatha, the younger Sri Dolagovinda: both find supreme bliss in the service of Sri Krishna.
One day Sriman Raghunatha said to Me: 'How will the word of Veda-Vyasa come true?
(It is said that) in the age of Kali the eighty-four hells will be filled; but Sri Krishna Chaitanya has closed that road —
by the great mantra of the name of Hari He has delivered the souls. Tell me: how will the hells be filled?'
Hearing this, Sri Dolagovinda laughed and said: 'They will be filled with all the sinners who hate Gaura.'
Hearing such words, I was amazed, and since then I know that both are incarnations of gods.
Blessed is My Krishnadasa, blessed are his sons: they are worthy of the service of Sri Madana-Gopala.
He is My own who worships Gauranga: he is fit to serve the treasure of My life.
Therefore I wish to entrust this service to Krishna Mishra. What is your wish?"
Hearing this, Sri Achyuta joyfully said, joining his palms: "As You have commanded, so I too think."
Then Sri Advaita said to Krishna Mishra: "Madana-Gopala is the Lord of My life.
Serve Him with devotion every day; do not allow those turned away from Him to worship Him.
Know that the averse are unbelievers, heretics, Advaitin sannyasis, yogis and jnanis,
those desiring enjoyment and liberation, devoid of the desire for devotion: these non-Vaishnavas I regard as averse to Krishna.
Among Vaishnavas, one who is outside a sampradaya, and among those of a sampradaya, one who does not acknowledge Gauranga —
he is surely averse to Krishna — this I shall determine. And one more word of Mine, listen, Krishnadasa:
those of My own who are evil-minded, who, transgressing My command, go their own way and do not acknowledge Gora —
(know:) Sri Gauranga is My Lord, I am His servant, the dust of His holy feet is My food.
Gora is the Lord of My life, Gora is the One I worship: whoever does not acknowledge that Gauranga is rejected by Me.
Those averse to Krishna are all in a low refuge: they are never fit to serve the Deity (sri-vigraha) of Krishna.
Whoever preserves the true dharma of his father is the real son — such is the word of the Vedas."
Having said this, He insistently entrusted the Deity of Sri Madana-Gopala to Krishna Mishra.
Having received the service of Krishna, Krishna Mishra in the bliss of love prostrated himself at the Lord's lotus feet.
With humble praise he bowed at his mother's feet, and Sita and Advaita both blessed him.
Then he humbly bowed to Sri Achyuta; Achyuta said: "I offer myself to your good fortune.
Krishna wished to show you mercy and revealed that wish through His own devotee,
as Krishna revealed the Vedas through Brahma" — and having said this, he embraced Krishna Mishra.
Gopala said: "Krishna is most merciful: by His mercy He will bring good to the whole family,
as when one waters the root of a tree, the branches, leaves and the rest are filled with joy."
"What good fortune!" — having said this, he bowed to Krishna Mishra, and Krishna Mishra embraced him tightly.
But the Acharya's other sons — Master Balarama and the very mighty Master Jagadisha —
in anger, after consulting with their people, diligently procured another Deity of Krishna,
performed the bathing ceremony and installed that Deity, and held a festival with their own people.
The pastimes of Sri Advaita are an impassable ocean: I have proclaimed only a drop of their essence.
Placing his hope in the feet of Sri Chaitanya and Sri Advaita, Ishana Nagara tells the Advaita-prakasha.

nityananda-vamsha.title: Бездетный брахман Судхамая из Махеша в Пури; Океан вручает ему девочку Нараяни
nityananda-vamsha.summary: Судхамая (Мукхути), зять Пипилая, с женой Видьюнмалой, раздав имущество брахманам, идёт с паломниками на Чандана-ятру в Нилачалу, проводит там Ратха-ятру и чатурмасью и поселяется в шалаше на берегу океана; Океан является во плоти и вручает им девочку Нараяни — Лакшми, переданную ему Гангой: её мужем станет сын Нитьянанды Вирачандра, сам Гауранга, который вскоре придёт сюда.

verses.text:
Жил в Махеше брахман с чистым сердцем;
почитание Вишну и вайшнавов было его ежедневным делом.

Звали его Судхамая, он был зятем Пипилая*;
жену его звали Видьюнмала.
notes: Махеш — селение на Ганге (Хугли) с древним храмом Джаганнатхи. Пипилай — Камалакара Пипилай, один из «двенадцати пастушков» (двадаша-гопала) спутников Нитьянанды.

verses.text:
Преданная Вишну, чистая, верная мужу женщина
всегда стояла подле супруга со сложенными ладонями.
[с. 31]

«Нет у меня ни дочери, ни сына — жизнь проходит напрасно.
Какая радость жить в мирской жизни, ради какой привязанности?»

Мукхути* ответил: «Верная жена, и у меня на душе то же:
я связан домом — правду тебе говорю.
notes: Мукхути — бенгальская фамилия (Мукхопадхьяя); так автор называет Судхамаю. Первая строка двустишия в обеих копиях испорчена; переведено по смыслу.

verses.text:
Вместе с паломниками, что идут на Чандана-ятру Господа*,
пойдём и мы взглянуть на Шри Мукунду.
notes: Чандана-ятра — летний праздник Джаганнатхи в Пури, когда божество умащают сандалом. Мукунда — здесь Джаганнатха.

verses.text:
По его милости это пришло тебе на ум.
Пойдём же, увидим Джаганнатху».

Сказав так, лучший из брахманов воскликнул имя Хари,
и Судхамая погрузился в океан блаженства.

На пятый день он пригласил брахманов своей деревни
и накормил их четырьмя родами яств*.
notes: Четыре рода пищи: та, что жуют, глотают, слизывают и сосут.

verses.text:
Всё добро, что было в доме, он раздал брахманам,
и каждого почтил гирляндой и благовониями.

В это время пришли все паломники,
и на великом празднике их угостили.

Поднявшись на рассвете, лучший из брахманов вместе с женой
отправился в путь с вайшнавами, радуясь беседам о Хари.

Оставшееся имущество — деньги и драгоценности, что ещё были, —
он взял с собой, чтобы поднести на трапезу Джаганнатхи.

Шаг за шагом пришли они в Нилачалу;
восклицая «Хари, Хари!», не знали дорожной усталости.

Узрев прекрасный лик Господа, он счёл свою жизнь исполненной
и обошёл все святые места.

С великой радостью он побывал на празднике колесниц,
и всё, что у него было скоплено, истратил на празднество.

Пробыв там чатурмасью* и обходя святые места,
он сказал своей жене такие слова:
notes: Чатурмасья — четыре месяца сезона дождей, когда странники остаются на одном месте.

verses.text:
«Пойдём в уединённое место, на берег океана,
будем совершать садхану, чтобы обрести Лучшего из Ядавов».

Придя туда, они устроили маленький шалаш из листьев,
и оба непрестанно повторяли имя Мурари.

Долгое время спустя, довольный их медитацией, Океан
явился к ним, приведя с собой девочку.

Приняв видимый облик, милостивый Океан
поставил девочку перед брахманом и кротко сказал:

«Возьми эту девочку и заботливо её расти:
через неё ты обретёшь драгоценнейшего из мужей.

Через эту девочку будет спасён твой род,
через эту девочку ты переправишься через океан мирской жизни.

Эта девочка по имени Нараяни — сама Лакшми;
Ганга вручила её мне, а я по милости отдаю её тебе.

Жених для неё не найдётся во всех трёх мирах:
энергия Господа достойна лишь Господа».

Брахман сказал: «Я — нищий брахман.
Как смогу я растить Лакшми?»

Океан сказал: «Брахман, не бойся.
Это не дурной сон — это правда*.
notes: Вторая строка повреждена в обеих копиях («duḥsvapna nahe … ei haẏa»); перевод по смыслу.

verses.text:
Она будет зримо жить с тобой, покорённая твоей любовью,
и непрестанно будет думать о своём Господе.

Он — сам Гауранга, Вишну, обитель вселенной;
он сын Нитьянанды*, и имя ему — Шри Вирачандра.
notes: Букв. «рождённый после Нитьянанды» (anuja), здесь — сын.

verses.text:
Вскоре, обходя святые места, он придёт сюда,
возьмёт эту девочку в жёны и сделает тебя счастливым».

Сказав так, Океан исчез,
а брахман и его жена исполнились радости.
[с. 32]
«Когда же Вирачандра Прабху явит нам себя?» —

verses_en.text:
In Mahesh there lived a brahmana of pure heart;
the worship of Vishnu and the Vaishnavas was his daily duty.

His name was Sudhamaya; he was the son-in-law of Pipilai*,
and his wife was named Vidyunmala.
notes: Mahesh is a village on the Ganga (Hooghly) with an old Jagannatha temple. Pipilai is Kamalakara Pipilai, one of Nityananda's "twelve cowherds" (dvadasha-gopala).

verses_en.text:
Devoted to Vishnu, pure, faithful to her husband,
she always stood by her husband with joined palms.
[p. 31]

"I have neither daughter nor son — my life passes in vain.
What joy is there in staying in worldly life, and for the sake of what attachment?"

The Mukhuti* replied: "Faithful wife, my mind is the same:
I have been bound to the house — I tell you the truth.
notes: Mukhuti is a Bengali surname (Mukhopadhyaya); the author uses it for Sudhamaya. The first line of the couplet is corrupt in both copies; translated by sense.

verses_en.text:
With the pilgrims going to the Lord's Chandana-yatra*
let us go too, to see Sri Mukunda.
notes: Chandana-yatra is the summer festival of Jagannatha in Puri, when the deity is anointed with sandalwood paste. Mukunda here means Jagannatha.

verses_en.text:
It is by his mercy that this has arisen in your heart.
Come, let us go and see Jagannatha."

Saying this, the best of brahmanas called out the name of Hari,
and Sudhamaya floated in an ocean of bliss.

On the fifth day he invited the brahmanas of his village
and fed them with the four kinds of food*.
notes: The four kinds of food: what is chewed, swallowed, licked and sucked.

verses_en.text:
All the goods that were in the house he gave away to the brahmanas,
and honored each of them with garlands and fragrances.

At that time all the pilgrims arrived,
and at a great festival they were fed.

Rising at dawn, the best of brahmanas, taking his wife along,
set out with the Vaishnavas, delighting in talk of Hari.

The rest of his property — whatever money and jewels remained —
he took with him for the offering of food to Jagannatha.

Step by step they came to Nilachala;
calling "Hari, Hari!" they felt no weariness on the road.

Seeing the Lord's beautiful face, he felt his life fulfilled,
and he went round all the holy places.

He took great joy in the festival of the chariots,
and whatever he had saved he spent on the festivities.

Staying there for the chaturmasya* and visiting the holy places,
he said these words to his wife:
notes: Chaturmasya: the four months of the rainy season, when wanderers stay in one place.

verses_en.text:
"Let us go to a solitary place on the shore of the ocean
and perform sadhana to attain the Best of the Yadus."

Going there, they made a small hut of leaves,
and both of them chanted the name of Murari without cease.

After a long time, pleased with their meditation, the Ocean
came to them, bringing a girl with him.

Taking on a visible form, the kindly Ocean
set the girl before the brahmana and gently said:

"Take this girl and raise her with care;
through her you will gain the jewel among men.

Through this girl your family will be delivered;
through this girl you will cross the ocean of worldly life.

This girl, named Narayani, is Lakshmi herself;
Ganga entrusted her to me, and I give her to you out of mercy.

No groom in the three worlds is worthy of her:
the Lord's energy is fit only for the Lord."

The brahmana said: "I am a very poor brahmana.
How will Lakshmi be raised by me?"

The Ocean said: "Brahmana, do not fear.
This is no bad dream — it is the truth*.
notes: The second line is damaged in both copies ("duḥsvapna nahe … ei haẏa"); translated by sense.

verses_en.text:
She will live with you visibly, won over by your affection,
and will think of her Lord without cease.

He is Gauranga himself, Vishnu, the abode of the universe;
he is Nityananda's son*, and his name is Sri Virachandra.
notes: Literally "born after Nityananda" (anuja), here meaning son.

verses_en.text:
Soon, while visiting holy places, he will come here,
take this girl as his wife and make you blessed."

Saying this, the Ocean vanished,
and the brahmana and his wife were filled with joy.
[p. 32]
"When will Virachandra Prabhu grant us his sight?" —

bhakti-ratnakara.title: Женитьба Вирачандры на Шримати и Нараяни, дочерях Ядунанданы Ачарьи из Джхаматпура
bhakti-ratnakara.summary: Странствуя по селениям, Джахнава приходит в Джхаматпур близ Раджбалхата, в дом слуги, где живёт брахман Ядунандана Ачарья, ставший по её милости преданным; по её желанию он отдаёт обеих дочерей, Шримати и Нараяни, Вирачандре; Вирачандра делает Ядунандану учеником, Джахнава принимает в ученицы обеих невест; Вирачандра, неотличный от Чайтаньи (по ГГД — Пайодхишайи, вьюха Санкаршаны), возвращается в Кхардаху, Васудха радуется невесткам.

verses.text:
В какие бы селения ни приходила Ишвари —
удачу всех тех селений не описать.

В Джхаматпур близ Раджбалхата
Ишвари пришла в дом одного слуги.*
notes: Раджбалхат — селение в нынешнем округе Хугли; Джхаматпур близ него, по-видимому, не тот Джхаматпур, что родина Кришнадаса Кавираджи (округ Бардхаман).

verses.text:
Там живёт брахман Ядунандана Ачарья;
по милости Ишвари он исполнился бхакти.*
notes: Ядунандана Ачарья из Джхаматпура — тесть Вирачандры (253); не путать с Ядунанданой Чакраварти и Ядунанданой из Кантака-нагара (таранга 9).

verses.text:
Жена Ядунанданы — по имени Лакшми;
что и говорить — она в высшей мере хранит долг верной жены.

У него две дочери — Шримати и Нараяни;
изящество их тел — предел красоты.*
notes: Шримати и Нараяни — жёны Вирачандры; эта Нараяни — не мать Вриндавана Даса.

verses.text:
По желанию Шри Ишвари этот счастливый брахман
отдал обеих дочерей Прабху Вирачандре.

Во время свадьбы было великое веселье;
Вирачандра сделал Ядунандану [своим] учеником.

Джахнава Ишвари, сильно возликовав,
сделала Шримати и Шри Нараяни — обеих — [своими] ученицами.

Свадьбу Вирачандры видели счастливцы;
кто сумеет описать красоту той свадьбы?

Сын Нитьянанды, исполненный великого сияния,
телом неотличный от Чайтаньи, чарующий мир.

Так [сказано] в «Шри Гаура-ганоддеша-дипике»:
Тот, кто есть вьюха Санкаршаны по имени Пайодхишайи, —
он и явился как Вирачандра, телом неотличный от Чайтаньи.*
notes: Пайодхишайи («возлежащий на океане») — Кширодакашайи Вишну; вьюха — проявление.

verses.text:
Женившись, Вирачандра вернулся домой;
видя невесток, Васу[дха] преисполнилась великой радости.
В селении Кхардаха все ликовали;

verses_en.text:
Whatever villages Ishvari went to —
the good fortune of all those villages cannot be described.

To Jhamatpur near Rajbalhat
Ishvari went, to the house of a servant.*
notes: Rajbalhat is a village in present-day Hooghly district; the Jhamatpur near it is apparently not the Jhamatpur that was the birthplace of Krishnadasa Kaviraja (Bardhaman district).

verses_en.text:
There lives the brahmana Yadunandana Acharya;
by the mercy of Ishvari he became full of bhakti.*
notes: Yadunandana Acharya of Jhamatpur is Virachandra's father-in-law (253); not to be confused with Yadunandana Chakravarti or Yadunandana of Kantaka-nagara (Taranga 9).

verses_en.text:
Yadunandana's wife is named Lakshmi;
what to say — hers is the utmost dharma of a chaste wife.

He has two daughters — Shrimati and Narayani;
the grace of their limbs is the utmost limit of beauty.*
notes: Shrimati and Narayani are the wives of Virachandra; this Narayani is not the mother of Vrindavana Dasa.

verses_en.text:
By the wish of Sri Ishvari that fortunate brahmana
gave both daughters to Prabhu Virachandra.

At the time of the wedding there was great festivity;
Virachandra made Yadunandana [his] disciple.

Jahnava Ishvari, greatly rejoicing,
made Shrimati and Sri Narayani — both — [her] disciples.

The fortunate saw Virachandra's wedding;
who could describe the splendor of that wedding?

Nityananda's son, full of great splendor,
his body non-different from Chaitanya, enchanting the world.

Thus [it is said] in the Sri Gaura-ganoddesha-dipika:
He who is the vyuha of Sankarshana named Payodhishayi —
he himself appeared as Virachandra, his form non-different from Chaitanya.*
notes: Payodhishayi ("He who lies on the ocean") is Kshirodakashayi Vishnu; a vyuha is an expansion.

verses_en.text:
Having married, Virachandra came home;
seeing her daughters-in-law, Vasu[dha] was filled with great joy.
In the village of Khardaha everyone rejoiced;

prema-vilasa.title: [Указатель к в. 24] Вирачандра женится на Шримати и Нараяни, дочерях Ядунанданы из Джхаматпура
prema-vilasa.summary: Вирачандра женится на двух дочерях Ядунанданы из Джхаматпура — Шримати и Нараяни; у него рождаются три сына и дочь.

verses.text:
Дочери Ядунанданы, жителя Джхаматпура, —
Шримати и Нараяни, блаженные красотой.
На обеих дочерях женился Вирачандра;

verses_en.text:
The daughters of Yadunandana, a resident of Jhamatpur,
Srimati and Narayani, blessed with beauty —
Virachandra married both daughters;

prema-vilasa.title: Женитьба Вирачандры на Шримати и Нараяни; его дети
prema-vilasa.summary: Ядунандана из Джхаматпура, из рода Пиппали, отдаёт Вирабхадре дочерей Шримати и Нараяни; у Вирачандры три сына — Гопиджанаваллабха, Рамакришна, Рамачандра — и дочь Бхуванамохини, жена Парватинатхи Мукхути из Пхулии.

verses.text:
Слушайте, слушайте, слушатели, всем сердцем:
опишу женитьбу Вирабхадры.

Житель Джхаматпура Шри Ядунандана —
у него были две очень красивые дочери:

старшая — Шримати, младшая — Нараяни,
благословенные красотой, достоинствами и нравом, чарующие мир.

Тот удачливый брахман, из рода Пиппали,
отдал обеих дочерей Прабху Вирабхадре.

В «Вирачандра-чарите» весьма подробно
описал я эту свадьбу с радостью в сердце*.
notes: По другим источникам (ср. глоссарий: Нараяни и Вишнуприя) жёны Вирачандры названы иначе; здесь — Шримати и Нараяни, дочери Ядунанданы из Джхаматпура. Сыновья Гопиджанаваллабха, Рамакришна и Рамачандра известны и по другим источникам.

verses.text:
У Вирачандры — одна дочь и трое сыновей;
я назову их всех по имени:

старший — Гопиджанаваллабха, средний — Рамакришна,
младший — Рамачандра, превосходный во всём.
Имя дочери — Бхуванамохини;

verses_en.text:
Listen, listen, O hearers, with one mind:
I shall describe Virabhadra's marriage.

A resident of Jhamatpur, Sri Yadunandana,
had two very beautiful daughters:

the elder Srimati, the younger Narayani,
blessed in beauty, virtue and character, enchanting the world.

That fortunate brahmana, of the Pippali family,
gave both daughters to Prabhu Virabhadra.

In the Virachandra-charita I have described
this wedding in great detail with joy in my heart*.
notes: In other sources (cf. the glossary: Narayani and Vishnupriya) Virachandra's wives are named differently; here they are Srimati and Narayani, daughters of Yadunandana of Jhamatpur. The sons Gopijanavallabha, Ramakrishna and Ramachandra are known from other sources as well.

verses_en.text:
Virachandra has one daughter and three sons;
I shall tell all their names:

the eldest is Gopijanavallabha, the middle Ramakrishna,
the youngest Ramachandra, excellent in every way.
The daughter's name is Bhuvanamohini;

nityananda-vamsha.title: Женитьба Вирачандры на Нараяни у Судхамаи; Вакрешвара посвящает царя Чакрадеву
nityananda-vamsha.summary: Вирачандра приходит в хижину Судхамаи, Нараяни узнаёт в нём своего Господа и гирлянда сама падает ему на шею; спутники называют родословную (сын Нитьянанды, внук Хадаи Бандьопадхьяи, готра Шандилья); приданое — пять харитаки; Океан в облике человека открывает брахману, что жених — Нараяна, тот же, что Джаганнатха, одаряет его драгоценностями, гандхарвы и Нарада приходят на свадьбу. Вакрешвара по велению Прабху даёт мантру Радхи-Кришны царю Чакрадеве из рода Гаджапати, и тот с войском провожает чету.

verses.text:
Дерево удачи лучшего из брахманов принесло плод:
утомлённый дорогой, Прабху пришёл в дом Судхамаи.

Увидев его, лучший из брахманов вместе с женой
силой этого даршана бросились обнимать его стопы.

Прабху поспешно стал их успокаивать:
«Что ты хранишь, брахман, — то и дай мне», — сказал он.

Брахман ответил: «Я — бедный и ничтожный.
Какое богатство я могу дать? Взгляни на мой дом».

Сказав так, он взял его за руку и ввёл в дом,
и там Нараяни, словно тень, увидела его*.
notes: «Чхая-рупа» — «подобная тени»: Нараяни тихо, незаметно смотрит на гостя.

verses.text:
Сидя в хижине из листьев, Лакшми, рождённая из вод,
служила Нараяне, поднося благовония и гирлянды.

«Сам Нараяна пришёл собственной персоной», —
поняла в глубине души Лакшми-деви.

«Это мой господин, владыка моей жизни», — уверилась она. —
«Кто, кроме моего Господа, может пленить моё сердце?»

Так Лакшми-деви подумала про себя, —
и гирлянда, которую она надела на шею Нараяне,

внезапно упала на шею Прабху.
Судхамая на разные лады читал ведийские гимны.

Прабху, придя со всеми своими спутниками,
остановился неподалёку, в деревне Чилка*.
notes: Чилка — селение близ Пури (у озера Чилика).

verses.text:
Брахман Судхамая пришёл и пригласил его,
и Прабху со спутниками принял трапезу в доме брахмана.

Тогда этот брахман, накинув ткань на шею,
обратился со смиренной просьбой к спутникам Прабху:

«Есть у меня девушка, рождённая из вод:
Океан дал её мне на воспитание.

Эта девушка достойна великого мужа.
Расскажите мне о нём и избавьте меня от страха.

Какого он рода, из какой деревни, чей сын?
Скажите мне без утайки и спасите меня».

Они сказали: «Нитьянанда — сын Хадаи Бандьопадхьяи,
из рода (готры) Шандильи, полная луна семьи Оджха*.
notes: Хадаи (Хадаи Пандит, Хадаи Оджха) — отец Нитьянанды. Шандилья — название готры; Оджха — «наставник», родовое звание.

verses.text:
У него один сын, имя ему — Вирачандра;
красотой, достоинствами, родом и нравом он всюду славен».

Так они рассказали о себе брахманам,
и все, радуясь в душе, говорили: «Хорошо, хорошо!»
[с. 36]

Услышав это, брахман обрадовался
и вместе с бывшими при нём брахманами назначил благоприятный час.

Брахман сказал: «В приданое я дам пять плодов харитаки».
Прабху ответил: «Да будет так», — и все дивились: «Что это, что это?»*
notes: Харитаки (миробалан) — плод; пять харитаки — символическое, нищенское приданое.

verses.text:
Час свадьбы пришёлся на сумерки — самое благоприятное время;
даже без жениховского наряда Прабху был пленителен как жених.

В это время Океан пришёл к брахману
и, приняв облик человека, сел в уединённом месте.

«Скажи, брахман, какой награды ты хочешь?
Что ещё сказать о пределе твоей удачи!»

«Всю жизнь я был […], а сегодня стал […]:
своими глазами я увидел чету Лакшми-Нараяны»*.
notes: Строка «janme(?) ati nimacchara āji macchara hainu» испорчена в обеих копиях; ключевые слова не восстановлены.

verses.text:
Океан сказал: «Брахман, смотри — вот он перед тобой:
полный Брахман, Нараяна, сам Господь.

Кто есть Джаганнатха — тот и есть этот облик:
чистое высшее блаженство, само воплощение радости».

Он вручил брахману бесценные драгоценности
и тотчас нагромоздил горы всевозможных яств.

Гандхарвы и киннары, Нарада и Тумбуру*,
приняв облик людей, все пришли в дом брахмана.
notes: Гандхарвы и киннары — небесные музыканты; Нарада и Тумбуру — божественные певцы.

verses.text:
Кто читал Веды, кто пел и играл на инструментах;
кто в облике богов, кто в облике людей — приходили и уходили.

Мохини нарядила Нараяни,
а наряд жениха пришёл и надел сам Океан*.
notes: Мохини — женский чарующий облик Вишну; здесь, возможно, просто «чаровница», небесная женщина.

verses.text:
Всё было готово, настали сумерки;
жених и невеста взглянули друг на друга и осыпали друг друга цветами.

Лучший из дваждырождённых произнёс великие слова
и отдал дочь в жёны в благоприятный час, в благоприятный миг*.
notes: «Великие слова» (махавакья) — формула отдачи дочери (каньядана).

verses.text:
Океан в своей сокровищнице, в божественных покоях,
уложил их обоих на ложе из цветов.

Оба, столь долго томившиеся в печали разлуки,
не могли насмотреться на лица друг друга.

Встав ясным утром, Прабху умылся,
пришёл к спутникам и благосклонно расспросил их.

Прабху велел Вакрешваре Пандиту*
и сказал такие слова: «Мы отправимся на родину».
notes: Вакрешвара Пандит — спутник Чайтаньи, славный танцор киртана.

verses.text:
Тот ответил: «Твоё слово я принимаю на голову»,
и, сказав так, отправился во дворец царя.

Правителем той страны был потомок Гаджапати,
грозной мощи, по имени Чакрадева*.
notes: Гаджапати — титул царей Ориссы. Чакрадева — правитель, иначе неизвестный.

verses.text:
Придя, Пандит явил свою силу,
и в сердце царя вскипел океан бхакти.

Он пал ниц, как палка, к его стопам
и снова и снова повторял: «Жизнь моя исполнилась».

«Смилуйся, дай мне мантру в уши!»
Совершив омовение и поклонение, они оба удалились в уединение.

Дав мантру Радхи-Кришны, Пандит сделал его своим,
и тогда царь сказал: «Я переправился через мирскую жизнь.

Что ты прикажешь?» — так говорил царь, сложив ладони;
из глаз его лились слёзы, и он снова и снова припадал к стопам.

Тот сказал: «Прабху совершил своё святое шествие сюда:
он взял в жёны дочь Судхамаи.
[с. 37]

С твоей помощью мы доставим чету на родину.
Ты будешь счастлив, увидев их, — скорее иди, раджа».

«Как прикажешь», — ответил царь, приняв повеление на голову,
и отправился в путь в великой поспешности.

Он взял с собой паланкины, слонов и колесницы,
и множество пеших воинов шло в полном снаряжении.

Придя, Пандит обо всём доложил Прабху
и добился для царя его милостивого взгляда.
Судхамая испросил желанный дар

verses_en.text:
The tree of fortune of the best of brahmanas bore fruit:
weary from the road, Prabhu came to Sudhamaya's house.

Seeing him, the best of brahmanas, together with his wife,
by the power of that sight went to clasp his feet.

Prabhu hastily calmed them:
"Whatever you have kept, brahmana, give that to me," he said.

The brahmana said: "I am very poor and wretched.
What wealth can I give? Look at my house."

Saying this, he took him by the hand and led him into the house,
and there Narayani, like a shadow, saw him*.
notes: "Chhaya-rupa," "like a shadow": Narayani watches the guest quietly, unnoticed.

verses_en.text:
Sitting in the hut of leaves, Lakshmi, born of the waters,
was serving Narayana with fragrances and garlands.

"That very Narayana has come in person" —
so Lakshmi Devi understood within her heart.

"This is my lord, the master of my life," she was certain. —
"Who but my Lord could captivate my heart?"

Thus Lakshmi Devi thought to herself, —
and the garland she had placed on Narayana's neck

suddenly fell upon Prabhu's neck.
Sudhamaya recited Vedic hymns in many ways.

Prabhu, coming with all his companions,
stayed nearby in the village of Chilka*.
notes: Chilka: a village near Puri (by Chilika lake).

verses_en.text:
The brahmana Sudhamaya came and invited him,
and Prabhu with his companions took his meal in the brahmana's house.

Then that brahmana, placing a cloth around his neck,
humbly petitioned Prabhu's companions:

"I have with me a girl born of the waters:
the Ocean gave her to me to raise.

This girl is worthy of a great personage.
Tell me about him and free me from fear.

Of what gotra is he, from what village, whose son?
Tell me without deceit and save me."

They said: "Nityananda is the son of Hadai Bandyopadhyaya,
of the Shandilya gotra, the full moon of the Ojha family*.
notes: Hadai (Hadai Pandita, Hadai Ojha) is Nityananda's father. Shandilya is the gotra; Ojha ("teacher") a family title.

verses_en.text:
He has one son, named Virachandra;
for beauty, virtues, lineage and character he is praised everywhere."

Thus they told the brahmanas about themselves,
